## C) Repair verification

S246-001: the plan's execution guardrail now names a portable sibling worktree rather than an identifying absolute path. Source and generated Markdown agree. A scoped plan-artifact scan found no absolute home-directory paths.

S246-002: cache_route_line now obtains its reason and fix through public_cache_reason. Known sidecar states receive fixed descriptions and repairs rather than sidecar-supplied text. Unknown states and reasons point to cache-proxy status without echoing their inputs. Transport failures retain only a fixed head; their retained repairs are fixed daemon strings, verified against the producers. Known daemon-built route/model reasons retain their established presentation. render::line still fences what is displayed.

The directory holder renderer uses the same projection for plain-route reasons and discards its fix. Proxied rows retain their fixed label; absent route data still adds nothing.

## D) Correctness and compatibility

No round-two change to spawn/revive dispatch, emit_seat_receipt, the success/JSON condition, raw-envelope handling or cheap-compaction sequencing. The projection borrows display text and does not mutate descriptor data. JSON therefore retains the original raw cache_proxy fields, while refusals and JSON output still add no receipt line.

No normal-use correctness regression found in the repair delta.

## E) Regression quality

the_receipt_line_never_shows_the_account_or_a_local_path checks exact identity-free output for account-bearing token/quota failures, path-bearing configuration/transport failures, an unknown state, an unknown reason and multiline forged text. The former verbatim renderer would retain those inputs and fail the new expected-output assertions; no executed mutation run is claimed.

The existing route-format test and directory-holder test also passed. As in round one, these unit tests do not independently prove both CLI receipt call sites; that bounded coverage limitation does not require new hardening or another review round.
